workingTitle: Molecular clouds may preserve a hidden microquasar's jet tracks
publicationStatus: Peer-reviewed PASJ Letter published online November 13, 2026
coreFacts: ALMA resolved numerous molecular filaments about 0.5 parsec wide and 10 to 20 parsecs long around HESS J1023−575 at an adopted distance of 7.5 kiloparsecs.
The filaments align with a 170-parsec jet and arc cloud system and match magnetohydrodynamic simulations in which a microquasar jet compresses atomic hydrogen into molecular gas.
Using gas density and gamma-ray luminosity, the authors estimate about 7 × 10^48 erg in cosmic-ray protons under a hadronic interpretation.
The inferred activity duration is 1 to 10 million years, but the compact engine remains hidden and could be a black hole or neutron star.

sources.label: ALMA: Footprints of High-Velocity Jets in a Molecular Cloud

verification.measured: ALMA mapped sub-parsec carbon-monoxide structure and found aligned filaments; H.E.S.S. supplied the gamma-ray morphology.
verification.inferred: Jet compression, the microquasar engine, proton energy, and long activity duration depend on simulations and a hadronic gamma-ray model.
verification.limitations: The compact source is not directly detected and may be either a black hole or a neutron star; the claim that it is the Milky Way disk's most powerful cosmic-ray accelerator is conditional.
